src/spinoct/analytic/uniaxial.py::0.1.reason: Dimensionless. The tolerance eps in the published definition of the 'optimal switching time' knee, T_eps = 2 ln(4/eps) (alpha + 1/alpha) tau0, at which Phi_m = (1 + eps) Phi_infinity. 0.1 is the value used in Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 177206 (2021) Fig. 3. It is a fraction of a cost ratio, so it carries no unit in any code path, and it is a named module constant that every caller can override.

src/spinoct/analytic/uniaxial.py::1e-12.reason: Dimensionless relative tolerance. It is compared against abs(t[0])/T, a ratio of two times, to decide whether a query grid begins at the initial time. It carries no unit of its own and only selects between the direct-on-grid integration path and the internal-grid fallback; the physics is identical either way.

src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::0.05.reason: Angle in radians (dimensionless). The default symmetry-breaking perturbation of the initial chain for a single solve. Radians are dimensionless and this is a small arc-length nudge, not a physical observable.

src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::0.15.reason: Angle in radians (dimensionless). The default symmetry-breaking perturbation for the multi-seed sweep, larger than the single-solve default because the sweep explores distinct basins. Not a physical observable.

src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::0.9.reason: Dimensionless. A unit-vector component threshold: if the start direction is nearly along x (component above 0.9) the reference axis for the antipodal bend is taken along y instead, to keep it non-parallel. Compares a component of a unit vector against a pure number.
src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::0.9.source: reference = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0]) if abs(start[0]) < 0.9 else np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])

src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::1.2.reason: Dimensionless line-search step-growth factor. After an accepted descent step the trial step size is grown by 20 percent so that long shallow descents do not crawl. It multiplies a step size, not a physical quantity, and carries no unit; the backtracking line search re-shrinks it whenever it overshoots.

src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::1e-06.reason: Angle in radians (dimensionless). The threshold within which the two endpoints count as antipodal, so the great circle is not unique and a bending axis is chosen. A geometric tolerance.

src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::1e-07.reason: Dimensionless. The central-finite-difference step for perturbing a unit-vector component in the tangent-gradient evaluation. It perturbs a component of a unit vector (magnitude at most 1) and the result is re-projected onto the sphere; it carries no physical unit.
src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::1e-07.source: step = 1e-7  # dimensionless perturbation of a unit-vector component, re-projected each step

src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::1e-09.reason: Angle in radians (dimensionless). The threshold below which two endpoint directions count as coincident, so the geodesic is a constant chain. A geometric tolerance, not a physical quantity.

src/spinoct/numeric/image_ocp.py::1e-12.reason: Dimensionless relative tolerance. Convergence when the relative decrease in cost between accepted steps falls below it, a ratio of two costs. Chosen relative precisely so it is unit-independent, unlike a gradient-magnitude tolerance.
